Deletion of commands with unchanged other-model survival
Finite-prefix completion with a proper fallback
conclusion: Every least-favourable prior has all coordinates at least delta=g/(2K), where T0=ceil(2B/c_min), g=(c_min/2)*r_min^T0, T1=ceil(2B^2/(c_min*g)), and K=c_max*T1+B.

claim_class: Effective arithmetic and finite-memory certificate built from the classification and the new explicit prior bound; no claim that prime factorization or common-power cycles are new.
classical_ingredients: Unique prime factorization
Bezout identity for primitive integer vectors
Counting lattice-coset points in bounded intervals
Real-algebraic quantifier elimination
conclusion: Finite saturation is decidable by positive rational collinearity of signed prime exponent vectors. In the saturating case compute r_i=t^h_i, choose J with t^(-J)>=tau_max/(delta*tau_min), and put N0=max(J,max h_i), N=(2N0+1)^(n-1), M0=1+nN. Then V_M0=V_hist and the history value is algebraic and computable through the inherited finite-M real-algebraic formula.

proof: Prime factorization converts rational log relations into exact integer power identities. A primitive exponent direction yields a rational common base. The explicit prior bound gives a computable lattice strip; each relative-score coordinate has at most 2*N0+1 values and each priority controller at most N states. Counted initialization adds one state to at most n disjoint tails. The inherited attained finite-budget semialgebraic frontier then computes the history optimum.
